evidence_items.summary: Misinformation is common in online media, including in health-related content. Such misinformation constitutes a significant risk to the medical-demographic security of the population. Many people actively seek medical information online without the ability to verify its trustworthiness. This paper proposes a modular system for automated detection of misinformation in medical content based on retrieval-augmented verification. In the pipeline, input articles are summarized and decomposed into atomic claims. Each claim is then vectorized using dense embeddings (BGE-Large-en-v1.5) and matched against a self-constructed knowledge base via cosine similarity to retrieve evidence. Retrieved evidence is verified using large language model (LLM)- based natural language inference (NLI) and aggregated into article-level predictions through a scoring function. The LLM used in the system is the open-source LLaMA-3.1 model with eight billion parameters. Together with a self-contained knowledge base, this represents a deliberately constrained environment. Such a setup isolates the contribution of the presented architecture from its dependency on external knowledge sources and LLMs with large parameter counts. The system achieved 98.4% accuracy and a macro F1 of 0.978 at 79.0% coverage on the evaluated datasets (DETERRENT and CONSTRAINT). This demonstrates that, even under resource constraints, the correct pipeline architecture enables high-precision misinformation detection on medical content. It also represents a clear improvement over the ablation experiment, which used the same model without the proposed pipeline and achieved an F1 of only 0.773.
evidence_items.title: Detecting Health Misinformation Using Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model

evidence_items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely used for question answering, summarisation, coding, and research support, yet choosing a suitable model remains difficult because models differ in performance, context capacity, cost, privacy, and deployment options. This paper presents a document-based comparative analysis of five LLMs: GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama 3.1 405B Instruct, and Mistral Large 2. Using published technical reports, official documentation, model cards, and recognised benchmark studies, the models are examined under a common framework covering response quality, reasoning, coding, language understanding, context-window capacity, speed, computational requirements, cost, privacy, and deployment flexibility. No new experiments are conducted, and results obtained under different evaluation conditions are not treated as directly equivalent. The analysis shows that model selection involves trade-offs: hosted models offer easier access, whereas models with downloadable weights give greater deployment control but require more computing resources. No single model is found to be best for every task, which supports a task-specific approach to selecting LLMs.
evidence_items.title: A Comparative Analysis of Large Language Models

organizations: Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology Delhi;
Lakshmi Narain College of Technology (LNCT), Bhopal
evidence_items.summary: Machine learning models for molecular discovery often train on bioactivity data from heterogeneous assays, yet assay context is rarely explicitly represented. We investigate whether natural-language assay descriptions provide predictive information beyond molecular and protein representations. We develop ACL-DTI (Assay-aware Contrastive Learning-based Drug Target Interaction) and MAMMAL-AsAP, an assay-context extension of MAMMAL-DTI. Across five triplet-disjoint random splits, assay-aware models achieve competitive or improved performance over assay-agnostic baselines. Among the evaluated models, MAMMAL-AsAP achieves the highest (R^2) of 0.7198 +/- 0.0085. Masking experiments show that ACL-DTI is robust to incomplete assay descriptions, exhibiting the smallest reductions in R^2 among the evaluated models when masking the target name, assay technique, or both: 0.0228 +/- 0.0064, 0.0406 +/- 0.0113, and 0.0620 +/- 0.0190, respectively. These results indicate that assay descriptions contain predictive information not fully captured by molecular structures and protein sequences, and reveal architecture-dependent differences in how this information is exploited.
evidence_items.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Assay-Aware Drug-Target Binding Affinity Prediction

organizations: Department of Orthopedics, Taizhou People’s Hospital
Department of Orthopedics, Taizhou Third People’s Hospital
The Affiliated Taizhou People's Hospital of Nanjing Medical University
evidence_items.summary: Background Large language model (LLM) chatbots are increasingly used by the public to obtain health information, but the safety and quality of their responses to questions about osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs) remain unclear. Objective To compare the safety and patient-facing response quality of four publicly accessible LLM chatbots when responding to standardized questions about osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures. Methods In this cross-sectional paired evaluation, 36 standardized OVCF-related patient-facing questions were submitted to each of four publicly accessible LLM chatbot interfaces—ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Doubao—in an initial response-generation round on June 20, 2026, from Jiangsu, China. Queries were conducted in English in independent single-turn sessions under matched conditions, yielding 144 responses for the primary between-chatbot analysis. A second independent generation round using the same 36 questions and matched query procedures was conducted 7 days later (June 27, 2026), yielding an additional 144 responses for within-model stability analysis. The questions covered symptoms and warning signs, diagnosis and imaging, conservative management, medication safety, rehabilitation, vertebral augmentation, fracture prevention, and special clinical scenarios. Five clinical raters, blinded to chatbot identity and generation round, independently evaluated safety, factual accuracy, empathic communication, treatment-related information quality using DISCERN, patient-information quality using EQIP, transparency using the JAMA benchmark criteria, and overall quality using the Global Quality Score. Readability was assessed automatically using six established indices. Between-chatbot comparisons and test–retest stability analyses used paired methods appropriate for the outcome type.
evidence_items.title: Performance of four large language model chatbots in responding to patient-facing questions about osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures: a cross-sectional paired evaluation

evidence_items.summary: Public opinion about artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly measured and invoked in debates about AI governance, yet heterogeneous survey items are often interpreted as indicators of one underlying attitude. Using a weighted survey of registered voters in the U.S. state of Pennsylvania (N = 929), this article tests whether four AI attitude and policy items form a coherent dimension and examines the correlates of a nervous-to-excited affect item. A principal-component analysis of polychoric correlations in the complete-case subset (N = 460) does not support a strong unidimensional scale. A companion sensitivity analysis of the three non-employment items on the larger available sample reproduces the same two-component pattern, so the negative scaling finding is not an artifact of the employment-contingent job item. A weak first component links excitement, lower job concern, and opposition to regulation, but reliability is low (ordinal alpha = 0.45; KMO = 0.48). An item asking whether the U.S. federal government is equipped to regulate AI loads separately and aligns more closely with evaluations of the named institution than with AI affect. Weighted regression with HC3 heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors, corroborated by multiple imputation with 20 datasets, shows that AI excitement is associated most strongly with personal AI use, followed by prospective economic optimism, age, and education. This ordering holds in both the listwise and multiply imputed specifications. The findings are bounded to this survey module, but they show why AI affect, behavioral exposure, policy preference, and institution-specific governance judgments should not be combined into an accidental scale without first establishing that they measure a common construct.
evidence_items.title: Testing the dimensionality of public attitudes toward artificial intelligence

evidence_items.summary: Otolaryngology is among the medical specialties most suitable for the application of artificial intelligence (AI), largely due to the wide variety of data generated in daily practice. Otoscopic and endoscopic images, voice recordings, audiological tests, vestibular assessments, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and digital pathology slides provide rich sources of information that can be analyzed using AI-based methods. As a result, AI has emerged as a valuable tool for tasks such as image classification, segmentation, risk prediction, outcome estimation, and optimization of clinical workflows. Despite growing scientific interest, however, many AI studies in otolaryngology remain at the developmental stage and have not yet undergone sufficient clinical validation for routine use. Currently, the most practical applications of AI involve well-defined and repetitive clinical tasks. These include supporting newborn hearing screening programs, predicting cochlear implant outcomes, interpreting otoscopic and nasal endoscopic images, assisting vestibular assessments, analyzing voice recordings for laryngeal disorders, and improving risk stratification in head and neck oncology. In contrast, complex clinical decisions that require comprehensive patient evaluation continue to depend on physician expertise, with AI functioning primarily as a supportive technology rather than an independent decision-maker. The future role of AI in otolaryngology is therefore not to replace clinicians but to enhance decision-making by improving efficiency, consistency, and data utilization. Successful implementation will require not only high diagnostic accuracy but also careful attention to validation, data quality, patient privacy, regulatory oversight, and clinical accountability. Consequently, the major challenge ahead is not the development of new algorithms, but their safe and responsible integration into clinical practice.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Otolaryngology: Current Status and Future Perspectives

evidence_items.summary: Broadband coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (BCARS) enables label-free hyperspectral chemical imaging, but weak signal components are often obscured by heteroscedastic noise. Here, we develop a physics-based variance stabilization transform and benchmark six hyperspectral denoising methods to identify effective strategies for BCARS noise reduction. The transform yields nearly intensity-independent noise variance while preserving the dispersive Raman response. Within this framework, we compare singular value decomposition, BM4D, Noise2Noise, deep image prior, self-supervised diffusion, and a cross-covariance-based singular value decomposition method (CCV) introduced here, using a shared phase-retrieval pipeline. Evaluation includes five simulated hyperspectral cubes with exact ground truth and experimental measurements of glycerol, polystyrene beads, and Caenorhabditis elegans. In simulations, variance stabilization reduces the ratio of maximum to minimum channel noise variance from approximately 72 to 1.2. Deep image prior and self-supervised diffusion achieve the highest mean foreground peak signal-to-noise ratios. CCV matches the mean foreground structural similarity of deep image prior with substantially shorter runtime and no per-cube rank tuning. Experimental comparisons reveal sample-dependent performance. These results establish physics-based variance stabilization as a common framework for adapting and evaluating hyperspectral denoisers for BCARS, with CCV offering a practical balance of reconstruction fidelity, computational speed, and automated operation.
evidence_items.title: Denoising broadband CARS hyperspectral images on variance-stabilized data: a unified benchmark

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Purpose The mechanical damage of red blood cells (hemolysis) remains a key challenge in the design of blood-contacting medical devices. This study aims to compare the predictive performance of the empirical power-law model and the physiologically motivated viscoelastic model in the FDA nozzle benchmark geometry, with a focus on how model parameters and shear stress definitions influence hemolysis predictions. Methods Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were performed using a finite volume framework to resolve flow fields and shear stresses in the FDA nozzle. Both hemolysis models were implemented under identical geometry, mesh and boundary conditions. A parametric analysis was conducted by varying key model parameters, including the viscoelastic constants A , $$T 1$$ T 1 , $$T 2$$ T 2 , the shear stress threshold $$\tau S$$ τ S , and the power-law parameters. Predictions were evaluated using both total shear stress and turbulent viscous shear stress (TVSS) formulations, and compared against experimental data. Conclusion The viscoelastic model demonstrated strong sensitivity to the relaxation time $$T 2$$ T 2 and to the choice of stress definition. A quasi-linear dependence on parameter A was identified, enabling calibration with experimental results. In contrast, the power-law model was less sensitive to stress definitions but strongly dependent on parameter fitting. The effect of $$\tau S$$ τ S differed between the two models: it reduced hemolysis in the power-law case but increased it in the viscoelastic formulation. Background The viscoelastic model offers a more mechanistic description of hemolysis but requires careful parameter calibration and is highly sensitive to stress definitions. The power-law model remains computationally efficient and easier to implement, though empirical by nature.
evidence_items.title: Comparative Evaluation of Power-Law and Viscoelastic Hemolysis Models in the FDA Nozzle Benchmark Geometry

organizations: Shanghai Key Laboratory of Maternal Fetal Medicine, Shanghai Institute of Maternal-Fetal Medicine and Gynecologic Oncology, Shanghai First Maternity and Infant Hospital, School of Medicine, Tongji University, Shanghai 200092, China
evidence_items.summary: Background: The four molecular subtypes of endometrial carcinoma defined by The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) can be reconstructed from multi-omics data, but these data contain about 460,000 features for 369 patients, the subtypes are imbalanced, and feature selection easily leaks test-set information. Methods: We developed POISE-X, a leakage-controlled, imbalance-aware benchmarking pipeline with an interchangeable metaheuristic search engine. Using RNA-seq, miRNA, DNA methylation, copy-number, mutation, and clinical data from 369 TCGA-UCEC patients, we compared 19 optimizers under nested five-fold cross-validation, with in-fold prefiltering to 2505 candidate features and a macro-averaged F1 fitness function. Results: Performance differed across optimizers in a Friedman test on fold means (p=1.989×10−6). No selected panel exceeded logistic regression on the full candidate pool, which reached a macro-averaged F1 of 0.902; the compact configuration chosen by our selection rule, POISE-GWO, retained 443 features with a macro-averaged F1 of 0.880, and the selection rule itself scored 0.881 under leave-one-fold-out evaluation, and an ANOVA-ranked panel of 450 features reached 0.886. These results held without clinical variables and, in the two searches tested, for parsimony weights of 0.8–0.99. A surrogate of the clinical molecular classification built from POLE exonuclease-domain mutation, mismatch-repair deficiency, and TP53 mutation reached a macro-averaged F1 of 0.924, higher on average than every multi-omics model. Conclusions: In this cohort, wrapper search therefore compressed the feature set without adding discriminative power, and the selected panels reconstructed an existing classification, not a new treatment-relevant signature. POISE-X is a framework for benchmarking feature-selection strategies; any selected panel requires external validation before clinical use.
evidence_items.title: A Leakage-Controlled Benchmark of Metaheuristic Multi-Omics Feature Selection for Reconstructing TCGA Molecular Subtypes in Endometrial Cancer

evidence_items.summary: BACKGROUND Timely cause-of-death (COD) information guides health policy, yet many deaths in low- and middle-income countries are not medically certified. In Africa, fewer than 10% of deaths are. Verbal autopsy (VA) yields a structured symptom questionnaire and a free-text narrative. Mortality surveillance increasingly records the narrative alongside the questionnaire, but the algorithms used to produce VA-based statistics were designed for structured responses only, so narratives inform physician COD assignment but do not contribute to algorithmic COD assignment. We evaluated whether supervised models could use both modalities to improve COD assignment. METHODS We analyzed 4,999 VA records for deaths at ages 12 years or older from a national sample of registered deaths in South Africa (RSA), using physician-assigned CODs as the reference standard. We trained unimodal and multimodal pipelines on the labelled records: pretrained language models (PLMs) fine-tuned on narratives alone, machine learning (ML) models on structured responses alone, and the two combined at the data, feature, and decision levels. We also prompted a locally deployed generative large language model (LLM) on the same unimodal and multimodal inputs, without parameter updates. All were compared with InSilicoVA, the operational comparator representing current automated practice. We evaluated individual-level assignment, population-level agreement, calibration, and generalization across provinces in RSA, reporting these metrics rather than ranking pipelines on any one of them. RESULTS Every supervised pipeline improved on InSilicoVA by 8.5-15.9 percentage points in top-1 accuracy and 3.5-7.1 points in cause-specific mortality fraction (CSMF) accuracy.
evidence_items.title: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence for Cause-of-Death Assignment From Verbal Autopsy Records: A National Benchmark Study in South Africa

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Accurate ground-based cloud classification is important for atmospheric monitoring, solar-energy forecasting, aviation weather assessment, and climate observation systems. However, reliable sky-image annotation is time-consuming, especially when cloud types are visually similar or mixed. In this work, we study the label efficiency of deep learning for ground-based cloud classification using the Ground-based Cloud Dataset (GCD). Rather than proposing a new architecture, we benchmark three practical learning strategies under limited annotation budgets: supervised transfer learning, uncertainty-based active learning, and high-confidence pseudo-labeling. An ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50 is used as a common frozen backbone, and experiments are repeated over five random seeds for label budgets ranging from \((1%)\) to \((100%)\) of the training labels. Supervised transfer learning is already highly label-efficient: test accuracy increases from \((0.635 \pm 0.018)\) with \((1%)\) labels to \((0.730 \pm 0.002)\) with \((40%)\) labels, approaching the full-label performance of \((0.735 \pm 0.003)\). Active learning and pseudo-labeling are competitive with supervised sampling and provide small improvements for some metrics and budgets, but neither produces a large or consistent aggregate gain. Diagnostic analyses show that accepted pseudo-labels are highly reliable, with accuracy ranging from \((0.946)\) to \((0.977)\), but are biased toward easier, high-confidence sky-type groups. In contrast, uncertainty sampling preferentially queries uncertain samples from visually challenging groups, including Mixed and the visually confusable Stratocumulus and Cumulonimbus groups, but these targeted acquisitions yield only modest performance improvements. Overall, these results show that transfer learning can substantially reduce annotation requirements for GCD, while simple active and semi-supervised strategies provide limited additional gains over a strong supervised baseline.
evidence_items.title: Label-Efficient Learning for Ground-Based Sky-Image Classification: A Benchmark of Transfer Learning, Active Learning, and Pseudo-Labeling on GCD

organizations: Department of Economics, Bukhara State University
Department of Economics and Management, Bukhara State Technical University
evidence_items.summary: Data-driven organizations increasingly depend on large, heterogeneous, and fast-moving data to sustain the quality of their products, services, and processes. The transition toward data-driven organizational quality, often discussed under the label of Quality 4.0, has so far been examined mainly through a managerial lens. As a result, the data foundations of that transition remain fragmented and under-theorized. This Conceptual Analysis reframes quality-oriented big data as a first-class data management problem and proposes a layered conceptual architecture that organizes the lifecycle of such data across five interconnected layers: multi-source acquisition, integration and fusion, data quality assurance, analytics and knowledge extraction, and data governance and ethics. The central argument is that data quality operates as a central mediating construct linking big data capability to organizational quality outcomes: analytics improves organizational quality in large part to the extent that the underlying data are accurate, complete, consistent, timely, and well governed. Drawing on the data management, data quality, and machine learning systems literatures, the article specifies the constituent elements of each layer, the dependencies among them, and the failure modes that arise when the data foundation is neglected. Five propositions and a structured research agenda position the acquisition, fusion, quality assurance, and governance of quality-oriented big data as priorities for data mining and management research. The architecture offers a data-centric vocabulary for designing and evaluating the data infrastructures on which data-driven organizational quality ultimately depends.
evidence_items.title: Managing quality-oriented big data: a conceptual architecture for acquisition, fusion, and analytics in data-driven organizations

evidence_items.summary: We develop an age- and immunity-structured COVID-19 model with setting-specific contacts, calibrated to Ontario incidence and hospital admissions before Omicron. We simulate counterfactual vaccination strategies and contact restrictions in schools, workplaces, and other community settings, evaluating projected severe-case demand against an illustrative healthcare-capacity benchmark. Vaccination combined with workplace and community contact restrictions keeps simulated demand within capacity. In contrast, relaxing restrictions in either setting produces large surges and repeated capacity threats, even when school restrictions remain. School-only changes produce smaller effects on severe disease. These findings highlight the value of vaccination and setting-specific contact restrictions that prioritize workplace and community settings for pathogens with adult-concentrated severe outcomes.
evidence_items.title: Vaccination and Non-School NPIs Shaped Ontario's Pre-Omicron COVID-19 Hospital Burden

evidence_items.summary: Palatal rugae are distinct anatomical ridges on the anterior part of the palate that exhibit individual-specific morphological patterns, making them valuable markers for personal identification and forensic analysis. With advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), deep learning methods have emerged as effective tools for extracting discriminative features from medical and biometric images. This study investigates the potential of transfer learning-based convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for biological sex classification using palatal rugae images captured through a smartphone camera. All pretrained models successfully learned discriminative biological sex -related features from palatal rugae images. Among them, Residual network 50 (ResNet50) and Visual Geometry Group 16 (VGG16) achieved the highest classification accuracy with optimal precision and recall, while EfficientNet-B0 and Dense Network 121 (DenseNet) demonstrated comparable but slightly lower performance. The Receiver Operating Curve (ROC curve) exhibited high Area under the Curve (AUC) values, confirming the strong separability between male and female classes. The findings confirm that smartphone-based imaging combined with transfer learning offers a promising, low-cost, and non-invasive approach for biological sex identification using palatal rugae patterns, as an adjunct tool for forensic odontology. Among the evaluated models, ResNet50 showed the most robust performance. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset and incorporating explainable Artificial Intelligence methods to support clinical and forensic applicability.
evidence_items.title: Smartphone-based biological sex identification from palatal rugae images: a comparative transfer learning study of pretrained convolutional neural networks

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Artificial intelligence is increasingly used for infectious disease surveillance, traveller risk assessment, outbreak forecasting and decision support. Travel creates a distinctive transportability problem because people move between epidemiological, geographic, climatic and healthcare contexts in which the conditions supporting an inference may change rapidly.


METHODS
This conceptual/theoretical methodological-development study was informed by a targeted narrative review of travel medicine, infectious disease surveillance, human mobility, border health, mass gatherings, antimicrobial resistance and health-AI validation literature.


RESULTS
We develop a mobility-conditioned admissibility framework that treats travel as movement across origin, transit, destination and return regimes. Interpretation is conditioned on mobility state, epidemiological regime, exposure history, time-dependent constraints and clinical or biological constraints. Five proposed operational states are retained: supported inference, conditionally transportable inference, active monitoring, restricted interpretation and withholding. The framework also distinguishes low probability from infeasibility and requires preservation of rare but epidemiologically feasible events.


CONCLUSIONS
Model availability and conventional predictive validity do not establish inferential transportability across changing travel contexts. Mobility-conditioned admissibility provides a complementary use-boundary layer for travel health AI by making cross-regime support explicit before outputs are interpreted or released. Its incremental value requires prospective evaluation against calibrated uncertainty, external validation and dataset-shift monitoring.
evidence_items.title: When Is Travel-Health AI Inference Transportable? Mobility-Conditioned Admissibility for Cross-Border Disease Risk and Decision Support.

evidence_items.summary: Understanding how humans interact with objects in complex visual scenes is fundamental to human-centric artificial intelligence. Yet, current Human-Object Interaction (HOI) detection frameworks often falter when faced with visual occlusions, vague interaction semantics, and scenarios that extend beyond predefined categories. We present Multi-View Context-Aware Disentangled Interaction Network (MCD-Inet), a unified framework designed to robustly detect HOIs under these challenging, open-world conditions. Our approach integrates a novel Multi-View Context Fusion mechanism that synthesizes fine grained spatial cues and broad semantic information across instance, interaction, and global levels. To decouple the learning of object localization from interaction semantics, we introduce a Disentangled Interaction Decoder, enabling clearer task specific representations. Complementing this, our Bilateral Knowledge Adaptation module bridges high-resolution spatial features from the visual backbone with abstract semantics from a pre-trained vision language model. To overcome the challenge of occluded interactions, we design an Occlusion-Robust Enhancement module, which extrapolates missing regions and mines contextual cues to recover interaction evidence. Finally, MCD-INet leverages multi-modal prompts incorporating both textual templates and visual exemplars to extend its detection capabilities to unseen HOI triplets. Extensive evaluations on HICO-DET, V-COCO, and the HICO-Ambiguous datasets confirm the superiority of our approach, achieving a new state-of-the-art mAP of 40.7% and demonstrating significant resilience in occluded and zero-shot scenarios. MCD-INet offers a powerful step toward generalizable, context-aware HOI detection in real-world visual environments.
evidence_items.title: Multi-view context learning for human-object interaction detection

evidence_items.summary: Recent advances in resting-state functional MRI have enabled non-invasive characterization of large-scale functional networks, providing novel biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring. Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI)—particularly resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) and graph-theoretical network analysis—has become the principal noninvasive method for characterizing addiction-related neuroplasticity in humans. This narrative review synthesizes fMRI evidence on addiction-related network reorganization across substance use disorders, including nicotine, alcohol, opioids, cocaine and other stimulants, and cannabis, as well as addiction-adjacent phenomena arising within primary neurological disease, with particular emphasis on impulse control disorders in Parkinson’s disease and substance-use vulnerability following traumatic brain injury. The review the rapidly evolving computational layer built on these findings, including graph neural networks, explainable artificial intelligence methods for biomarker attribution, multimodal foundation models pretrained on large unlabeled neuroimaging corpora, and federated learning and harmonization strategies designed to enable multi-site, privacy-preserving biomarker discovery. We also examine fMRI-guided neuromodulation, including repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, transcranial direct current stimulation, and deep brain stimulation, as both a mechanistic probe and a treatment strategy, and evaluate the reproducibility, generalizability, and clinical translation barriers that currently constrain this literature. We conclude with a precision-medicine roadmap emphasizing standardized acquisition and analysis pipelines, prospective longitudinal and multimodal designs, externally validated and explainable machine-learning biomarkers, and dedicated connectivity studies in understudied neurological-comorbidity populations. Realizing the clinical potential of fMRI biomarkers of addiction-related neuroplasticity will require moving from descriptive group-level neuroimaging findings toward reproducible, individually actionable, and mechanistically interpretable tools.
evidence_items.title: Functional MRI Biomarkers of Addiction-Related Neuroplasticity in Neurological Disorders: A Comprehensive Review of Functional Connectivity, Brain Network Reorganization, and Clinical Applications

evidence_items.summary: There is a growing need to leverage mathematical models of the central nervous system (CNS) with translational approaches employing in vitro-in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) approaches. As a benchmark of brain penetration, unbound brain partitioning (Kp,uu), and subsequently a combination of cerebral Open Flow Microperfusion (cOFM) and microdialysis (MD) were evaluated in rats. Additionally, a six-compartment physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of the CNS was developed in rats using six drugs with varying affinities to the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) transporter to learn and verify the in vivo studies. Active and passive drug efflux and permeability parameters derived from two P-gp overexpressing cell lines (MDCK-I and LLC-PK1) were scaled using proteomics-informed methods. Model predictions were evaluated with data obtained from terminal brain-to-plasma partition coefficient from both rat cOFM and MD experiments. In correcting for loss of drug in both the cOFM and MD equipment, a relative recovery (RR) showed significantly higher recovery in cOFM compared to MD experiments; for phenytoin, quinidine, and verapamil these were 0.53/0.063, 0.73/0.46, and 0.16/0.04 (cOFM/MD), respectively. Notably, higher P-gp efflux obtained from experiments with MDCK-I-transfected cells resulted in simulated lower drug concentrations in brain compartments. Overall, the CNS-IVIVE-PBPK model tended to overpredict brain drug concentrations, especially using data obtained from transfected LLC-PK1 cells. However, there is better agreement between the model predictions and the observed data for whole-brain concentrations obtained from terminal studies. We also demonstrated the feasibility of an IVIVE framework that integrates cell line derived passive and active drug parameters to estimate brain concentrations.
evidence_items.title: Translational Evaluation of In Vitro-to-In Vivo Extrapolation Techniques for Brain Penetration Using Open Flow Microperfusion and Microdialysis in Rats.

evidence_items.summary: Industrial internet of things (IIoT) environments connect devices, gateways, hosts, and services in ways that increase both operational visibility and cyber-attack exposure. Conventional intrusion-detection systems commonly produce flat attack labels and may underuse relational information between communicating assets. We investigate an ATT&CK-inspired stage-aware intrusion-detection framework that maps observed behaviour into four operational classes: Benign, Initial Access & Discovery (IAD), Lateral Movement, Execution & Persistence (LMEP), and Impact (IMP). Network-flow observations are represented using leakage-aware feature processing and an asset–time interaction graph, enabling comparison of feature-based, graph-based, temporal, and fusion models. To reduce dependence on a single benchmark, we evaluate the stage-aware formulation on both ToN-IoT and Edge-IIoTset. Following correction of the temporal-windowing pipeline, ToN-IoT contains 34,435 asset–window instances. GAT achieves the strongest ToN-IoT stage-detection performance with Macro-F1 0.687±0.041\documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$0.687\pm 0.041$$\end{document}, followed by GraphSAGE (0.671±0.015\documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$0.671\pm 0.015$$\end{document}) and GCN (0.660±0.039\documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$0.660\pm 0.039$$\end{document}). The logistic-regression RF–GCN stack reaches 0.395±0.067\documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$0.395\pm 0.067$$\end{document} and does not outperform the strongest graph learners. A controlled meta-learner ablation increases stacked Macro-F1 to 0.468 with gradient boosting, suggesting that meta-learner choice contributes substantially to the fusion shortfall. On Edge-IIoTset, the feature-based Random Forest performs best with Macro-F1 0.615. We additionally evaluate stage-mapping sensitivity, graph construction, window-size sensitivity, alternative stacking meta-learners, baseline tuning, bootstrap uncertainty, and inference latency. We formulate a strict leakage-controlled pre-impact forecasting protocol; however, although the corrected ToN-IoT representation yields 21,313 candidate forecasting instances, only five are positive and all occur in the training partition, with zero positives in validation and test. We therefore do not report held-out forecasting-performance estimates and limit our empirical claims to stage-aware intrusion detection.
evidence_items.title: Multi-stage attack detection in IIoT supply chains using graph neural networks

evidence_items.summary: Ensuring the quality and credibility of medical education systems increasingly depends on robust accreditation mechanisms, yet the performance of accreditation bodies themselves often remains insufficiently evaluated. Addressing this gap, this study developed and validated the first national meta-accreditation standards for Iran’s Ministry of Health and Medical Education. Using a rigorous mixed-methods design, the study integrated insights from semi-structured interviews with 13 national experts, a comparative review of six international recognition systems, expert panel consensus, and a national survey of 90 stakeholders. From an initial pool of 184 standards, systematic refinement led to a final set of 51 standards. Stakeholder evaluation demonstrated strong consensus across practicality, necessity, and transparency (76–94%), with all standards exceeding the predefined 70% agreement threshold. The resulting framework is structured across three domains: structure and formality, accreditation processes, and accountability and quality improvement. By aligning national needs with international benchmarks, these standards enhance transparency, consistency, and trust in accreditation systems. The high level of expert agreement and methodological rigor underscore the framework’s readiness for implementation and its potential as a model for strengthening meta-accreditation in similar centralized health education systems.
evidence_items.title: Developing national meta-accreditation standards for medical education accreditation bodies in Iran: a mixed-methods standards development and consensus study

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) carries a substantial mortality burden and risk of long-term morbidity. Although prior investigations have demonstrated an inverse association between SAH admission volume and in-hospital mortality, reported thresholds remain broad. Importantly, the relative importance of both admission and procedural volume has yet to be evaluated on a national scale. We examined the association of volume metrics with outcomes in an SAH cohort.


METHODS
All adult (≥18 years) hospitalizations with a primary diagnosis of nontraumatic SAH were identified from the 2016 to 2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Multivariable regression models were developed to evaluate the independent and joint associations of SAH admission and clipping and coiling procedural volume with in-hospital outcomes.


RESULTS
Of an estimated 142 271 hospitalizations, index mortality was 20.2%. Following risk adjustment, both increasing SAH admission volume and clipping and coiling procedural volume were independently associated with reduced mortality. When modeled jointly, however, clipping and coiling procedural volume remained an independent predictor of mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 0.981 per 10 procedures, P<0.001) whereas SAH admission volume was no longer significant (P=0.40).


CONCLUSIONS
Joint examination of SAH and clipping and coiling procedural volume revealed procedural caseload to be the dominant predictor of in-hospital mortality, suggesting that survival benefits historically attributed to admission volume may be more precisely explained by procedural expertise. These findings support reexamination of volume-based benchmarks in contemporary cerebrovascular care frameworks.
evidence_items.title: Contemporary Analysis of the Volume-Outcome Relationship for Patients With Nontraumatic Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.

evidence_items.summary: Ultra-small, atomically precise gold nanoclusters (Au NCs) offer distinctive opportunities for electrocatalysis owing to their discrete electronic structures and high density of coordinatively unsaturated sites; however, uncontrolled aggregation and the absence of spatial control over cluster nucleation on conventional supports remain significant challenges for the rational engineering of catalytic interfaces. Herein, we report a site-directed, in situ strategy for the spatially controlled synthesis of Au NCs on DNA origami (Au NC@DNA) scaffolds, which function as localized nucleation and coordination platforms to afford Au NC@DNA origami hybrid architectures. The resulting hybrids exhibit a narrowly distributed Au NC size of 1.5 ± 0.2 nm, as established by complementary UV-vis and fluorescence spectroscopy, atomic force microscopy (AFM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). When evaluated for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in 0.5 M H2SO4, the Au NC@DNA origami hybrid exhibits a low overpotential of 87 mV at a current density of -10 mA cm-2, together with a Tafel slope of 67 mV dec-1, a charge-transfer resistance of 13.87 Ω, and a mass activity of 416.3 A g-1. These electrocatalytic metrics substantially exceed those of Au NC@Poly-C, pristine DNA origami, and poly-cytosine (poly-C) controls and approach the performance of the benchmark Pt/C catalyst. Furthermore, the Au NC@DNA origami catalyst demonstrates pronounced operational durability, maintaining its electrocatalytic activity over 3000 continuous linear sweep voltammetry cycles and 36 h of chronoamperometric operation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations identify the DNA-Au21 configuration as a thermodynamically favorable catalytic motif, characterized by a near-thermoneutral Gibbs free energy of hydrogen adsorption (ΔGH*). Bader charge analysis and projected density of states (PDOS) further reveal substantial electronic coupling between the Au cluster and DNA ligand, accompanied by Au-H orbital hybridization and charge redistribution involving neighbouring N/O coordination sites. These results demonstrate that DNA origami functions not merely as a structural template but as an electronically coupled and catalytically relevant scaffold that modulates the physicochemical properties of atomically precise Au nanoclusters.
evidence_items.title: DNA origami as an electronically coupled scaffold for Au nanocluster electrocatalysts.

evidence_items.summary: Urban road-network vulnerability is difficult to assess when disruption probabilities are unknown and alternative paths perform differently under adverse network conditions. This study proposes a game-theoretic framework in which network users and an adversarial entity interact through a two-player non-cooperative zero-sum game. Users minimize expected travel cost by selecting mixed strategies over alternative paths, while the adversarial entity maximizes it by selecting mixed strategies over predefined disruption scenarios. The framework integrates alternative-path generation, scenario-specific travel costs from PTV VISUM, and linear programming to determine minimax equilibrium strategies. An application to 25 selected origin-destination pairs in the metropolitan road network of Naples, Italy, considers five road-closure scenarios and evaluates both physical disruption exposure and strategic importance. The results show that the disruption affecting the largest number of paths does not necessarily exert the greatest strategic influence on the equilibrium. Mixed user strategies emerge for 20 of the 25 origin-destination pairs and reduce worst-case travel cost relative to the best pure-path worst-case benchmark. Demand-weighted results further confirm that physical exposure and strategic importance provide distinct information on network vulnerability. From a practical perspective, the framework can support transport planners in distinguishing disruptions with broad physical impacts from those that exert greater strategic influence on path-choice strategies. The proposed framework therefore complements conventional disruption assessment by explicitly accounting for path diversification and strategic interaction without requiring predefined disruption occurrence probabilities.
evidence_items.title: A game-theoretic assessment of urban road-network vulnerability: a case study of Naples, Italy

evidence_items.summary: Workplace communication is commonly evaluated through information quality, channel effectiveness, and employee alignment, while its psychological and relational consequences receive less integrated attention. This study develops and pilot-tests the Positive Psychological Communication Framework (PPCF), which conceptualizes credible, respectful, strengths-aware, meaning-centered, participative, and behaviorally consistent communication as an organizational resource associated with employee voice, trust, engagement, and flourishing-related outcomes. The full theoretical PPCF integrates positive psychology, psychological safety, organizational trust, employee engagement, and strategic communication. The pilot study, however, tests a deliberately reduced empirical model: Inclusiveness and Voice represents only the voice-related aspect of relational safety, and Organizational Success serves only as a flourishing-related outcome rather than a complete measure of collective flourishing. A quantitative cross-sectional pilot study was conducted using 83 usable responses to a 27-item questionnaire comprising nine three-item dimensions. The data demonstrated good factorability (Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin = .885; Bartlett's chi-square = 1,649.49, p < .001). Internal consistency was acceptable to excellent for eight constructs, while Strength-Based Communication returned alpha = .643. A nine-factor confirmatory factor analysis showed acceptable but marginal fit, chi-square(288) = 437.34, CFI = .903, TLI = .882, and RMSEA = .080. In the reduced structural model, all four proposed paths were positive and statistically significant. The sequential indirect association from strategic communication to organizational success through inclusiveness and voice, trust, and engagement was .155, with a 95% bootstrap confidence interval [.026, .371].
evidence_items.title: Positive Psychological Communication at Work: Development and Pilot Testing of a Framework Linking Voice, Trust, Engagement, and Organizational Flourishing

evidence_items.summary: A synthetic (programmatically generated) teaching dataset accompanying the methodological manual "Digital Technologies in Educational Research" (Tsyfrovi tekhnolohii v naukovo-pedahohichnykh doslidzhenniakh; M. Pryhodii, Institute of Vocational Education of NAES of Ukraine, 2026). It is intended for Practical Class 6 on statistical processing, visualisation and reproducible analysis of pedagogical experiment data in the PhD programme in Professional (Vocational) Education. The data simulate a quasi-experiment in a vocational education institution: 101 learners in six study groups across two occupations (welder – 68, cook – 33); three experimental groups (n = 52; digital course with a simulator) and three control groups (n = 49). Variables include pre- and post-test scores (0–100), a 10-item learning-motivation Likert scale (1–5; items 3 and 7 reverse-keyed), an attention-check item, completion time, competence level before and after the experiment (1–4), and open-ended comments (in Ukrainian; 23 responses). The dataset deliberately contains typical data-quality issues for cleaning exercises: 9 failed attention checks, 2 implausibly short completion times, reverse-keyed items, and clustering of learners within groups. Suggested analyses: exclusion criteria, reverse coding, scale score and Cronbach's alpha, descriptive statistics, baseline equivalence, Welch's t-test / Mann–Whitney U with effect sizes, ICC and mixed-effects model, chi-square test for competence levels, thematic analysis of comments.   NOTE: All data are synthetic and do not relate to any real persons, groups or institutions; they must not be used to draw empirical conclusions.

evidence_items.summary: Phenmedipham (PMP), an herbicide registered for various crops across different geographies, is under re-approval in Europe and should be evaluated for potential endocrine-disrupting properties according to the current legislation on pesticide active substances. This paper describes an evidence-based assessment of potential thyroid-mediated effects of PMP in Xenopus laevis as model species for thyroid modality. As an indication of thyroid activity, rat thyroperoxidase inhibition was reported in a single in vitro assay in the US-EPA ToxCast database. The results of a 27-day Extended Amphibian Metamorphosis Assay with X. laevis showed very little evidence of the consequences of potential thyroperoxidase inhibition in vivo . A minor non-statistically significant delay of 0.76 days in the mean time to reach metamorphic climax was estimated for tadpoles from the highest treatment group (0.5 mg/L) which reached the metamorphic climax at a significantly lower rate over time compared to control. As it is within the historical control data variability (±2.72 days), the estimated developmental delay of 0.76 days is not adverse for individuals, and no population-level impact is therefore expected in field. Other statistically significant low-magnitude effects (e.g. ≤ 4.2% for reduced survival and growth) were observed at the highest PMP concentration at study termination. Minor statistically significant histopathological changes in the thyroid of tadpoles from the highest treatment group could be explained by the effects on developmental timing. Overall, the response pattern observed in X. laevis was consistent with generalised toxicity and thus, PMP does not meet the endocrine disruption identification criteria for thyroid modality.
evidence_items.title: Integrated evidence-based assessment of in vitro and in vivo data supports that the effects of phenmedipham in Xenopus laevis are consistent with generalised toxicity rather than thyroid disruption

evidence_items.summary: Introduction: While secondary intention healing and local flap reconstruction are standard for cutaneous defects, their combined dimensional kinetics remain poorly understood. Balancing wound contraction with structural stability requires comparative evaluation. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate and compare wound size changes between secondary intention healing combined with flap reconstruction versus secondary intention healing alone in cutaneous surgery. Material and methods: This single-blind randomized trial at Sina Hospital enrolled 20 patients (10 per group via convenience sampling) to compare secondary intention healing combined with local flap reconstruction versus secondary intention healing alone for cutaneous surgical defects, evaluating wound dimensional changes over 12 weeks. Results: Baseline defect area strongly predicted healing duration (r=0.872, R 2 =0.761, P=0.0010). Gender showed no significant differences in defect size (P=0.377) or healing time (P=0.066). Healing milestones occurred at 4 weeks (30%), 6 weeks (30%), and 8 weeks (40%). Conclusion: Initial surgical defect size is a primary determinant of cutaneous recovery kinetics, whereas gender exerts no confounding effect, supporting the clinical utility of defect-guided reconstructive planning and secondary intention management.
evidence_items.title: Secondary Intention Healing Combined with Flap Reconstruction Versus Secondary Intention Healing Alone in Cutaneous Surgery: A Comparative Analysis of Wound Size Changes

evidence_items.summary: Introduction: Cutaneous surgery requires balancing reconstructive durability with minimal morbidity. While secondary intention healing offers simplicity, expansive defects face prolonged recovery. Combining secondary intention with local flaps optimizes healing, yet the precise predictive role of initial defect size remains underexplored. This prospective study evaluates secondary intention healing with versus without local flap reconstruction, investigating how initial defect size predicts healing duration. Material and methods: This prospective, randomized, single-blind clinical trial at Sina Hospital evaluated twenty surgical patients (n=20) allocated equally into secondary intention healing alone versus combined local flap reconstruction. Participants were selected via convenience sampling based on strict eligibility criteria. Evaluated variables included baseline defect size, serial wound reduction kinetics measured planimetrically across twelve postoperative weeks, complete healing milestones, and postoperative pain intensity. Results: This prospective trial (n=20) demonstrates that baseline defect surface area strongly predicts healing duration (r=0.87, R 2 =0.760, P<0.001), while combined local flap reconstruction significantly accelerates early wound area reduction and milestone achievement (50% healed at week 4) compared with secondary intention alone. Conclusion: Initial surgical defect magnitude governs cutaneous recovery kinetics, whereas adjunctive local flap reconstruction successfully optimizes early tissue repair timelines, supporting defect-guided reconstructive decision-making in clinical practice without confounding gender influences.
evidence_items.title: Comparative Evaluation of Secondary Intention Healing with Versus Without Local Flap Reconstruction in Cutaneous Surgery: The Predictive Role of Initial Defect Size on Healing Duration

evidence_items.summary: Introduction: Seborrheic dermatitis of the scalp is a chronic inflammatory condition driven by microbial dysbiosis and aberrant host immunity. Because conventional topical therapies fail to address systemic drivers, targeting the gut-skin axis through microbial modulation presents a promising alternative. Therefore, this study investigated the therapeutic efficacy of oral probiotics in mitigating scalp desquamation induced by seborrheic dermatitis. Material and methods: This prospective randomized controlled trial conducted at Sina Hospital evaluated sixty-two patients with scalp seborrheic dermatitis. Participants were allocated into a control group receiving standard topical therapy (n=30) and an intervention group receiving adjunctive oral probiotics combined with standard topical treatment (n=32) over an eight-week period to assess clinical desquamation and therapeutic efficacy. Results: Despite a significant baseline difference in scalp desquamation severity between the control group (5.37 ± 2.56) and the intervention group (3.91 ± 2.26, P=0.02), follow-up evaluation at visit two demonstrated a markedly greater reduction in desquamation severity for patients receiving oral probiotics (0.94 ± 0.98) compared to conventional therapy alone (2.67 ± 2.05, P<0.001). Conclusion: Oral probiotic supplementation combined with conventional therapy significantly mitigates scalp desquamation severity in patients with seborrheic dermatitis compared to conventional treatment alone. Despite baseline disparities, the substantial post-intervention improvement highlights the therapeutic efficacy and clinical value of adjunctive probiotic administration in managing chronic inflammatory scalp conditions.
evidence_items.title: Therapeutic Efficacy of Oral Probiotics in Mitigating Scalp Desquamation Induced by Seborrheic Dermatitis

evidence_items.summary: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent anthropogenic contaminants widely detected in aquatic environments worldwide. Conventional wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are increasingly recognized as important emission sources due to the release of PFAS via effluent and the land application of biosolids. However, tracing PFAS mass flows and identifying the mechanisms governing PFAS changes across individual treatment compartments remain challenging, partly because parameters quantifying PFAS transformation and adsorption-desorption in the field are hard to measure. To address these problems, we developed the first native graphical user interface application, PFAS DT Investigator.v0, to assist researchers in investigating the distribution and transformation of PFAS in conventional WWTPs. This application integrates four main functions: (i) system information navigation; (ii) mass flow calculation; (iii) PFAS distribution and transformation analysis; and (iv) simulation of PFAS redistribution. Application evaluation demonstrates that this software is a robust tool for investigating PFAS distribution and transformation in conventional WWTPs.
evidence_items.title: PFAS DT Investigator v0

evidence_items.summary: Vitamin E and Zinc are essential dietary elements; they possess antioxidant effect that can control the free radicals which cause damage of the tissue. This study was done to evaluate the possible effects of vitamin E and zinc as natural antioxidant on ciprofloxacin-induced Achilles tendon damage in albino rats. Twenty adult male albino rats were used in this study and were randomly divided into 4 groups. Group I: control, group II: received ciprofloxacin (800 mg/kg/day) for 10 days. Group III: received the same dose of ciprofloxacin and vitamin E (100 mg/kg/days) for 10 days. Group IV: received the same dose of ciprofloxacin and zinc (50 mg/kg/day) for 10 days. Ciprofloxacin causes fragmentation of the tendoachilles with necrotic cells. Tendoachilles damaged by ciprofloxacin revealed multi vacuolated tenocytes detached from the matrix. The nucleus of tenocyte was condensed with irregularities of the nuclear membrane. Concomitant administration of vitamin E with ciprofloxacin was reducing lesions in Achilles tendon; Tenocytes had intimate contact with the matrix. The vacuoles were present in the cytoplasm were less than those treated with ciprofloxacin only. Zinc administration with ciprofloxacin reveals fewer lesions; tendons appear intact but there is a limited areas with necrotic cells & limited area with degenerated fibers. In conclusion, co-administration of vitamin E or zinc during ciprofloxacin therapy has a significant tendo-protective effect in a rat model of ciprofloxacin-induced tendon damage. Also alleviation of lesions by zinc is better than that of vitamin E. Thus zinc could be considered as a good tendo-protective agent against ciprofloxacin induced tendinopathy.
evidence_items.title: Histological Study Of The Role Of Vitamen E And Zinc On Tendenopathy Induced By Ciprofloxacin In Albino Rat

evidence_items.summary: Dataset Description This dataset supports the systematic literature review entitled “Impacts of Climate Change on International Trade, Competitiveness, and Supply Chains of Fisheries Commodities: A Systematic Literature Review.” The review followed the PRISMA 2020 reporting framework and used a PECOS-informed eligibility approach. Searches conducted in Scopus, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, and PubMed identified 707 records. After removing 44 duplicates, 663 records were screened, seven full-text articles were assessed for eligibility, and six studies were included in the final synthesis. The dataset contains structured information on study selection, study-level characteristics, climate-related stressors, fisheries trade and market outcomes, supply-chain disruptions, adaptation and resilience responses, methodological quality appraisal, and outcome-level evidence extraction. The dataset is provided to support research transparency, reproducibility, and further investigation of climate change impacts on international fisheries trade and seafood supply chains. Keywords: Climate change; Fisheries trade; Seafood supply chains; International trade; Systematic literature review; PRISMA 2020; Climate resilience.
evidence_items.title: Dataset Supporting a Systematic Literature Review of Climate Change Impacts on Fisheries Trade and Supply Chains

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a significant driver of digital transformation across global industries, although developing economies such as Iraq encounter distinctive challenges in realizing its full potential. This study examined digital transformation in Iraq from 2020 to 2024, focusing on the influence of digital infrastructure, human capacity, and governance on service efficiency, transparency, industrial productivity, and digital inclusion. A descriptive and analytical research design was employed, utilizing 105 secondary data points obtained from international and national sources. Correlation and regression analyses were conducted to evaluate the relationships between key factors and digital transformation outcomes. The findings indicate that service processing times decreased from 20 to 10 days, transparency scores increased from 25 to 35, industrial productivity improved from 1.5 to 4.5 percent, and internet penetration expanded from 48 to 65 percent. Correlation results demonstrated positive associations between digital transformation and infrastructure (0.78), human capacity (0.72), and governance (0.69), whereas contextual constraints exhibited a negative association (-0.55). Regression analysis identified infrastructure readiness as the strongest contributing factor (β = 0.41), followed by human capacity (β = 0.29) and governance (β = 0.22), while contextual constraints negatively influenced progress (β = -0.18). These findings highlight the importance of strengthening technological infrastructure, developing AI-related skills, and improving regulatory governance to accelerate digital transformation in Iraq. The study recommends expanding broadband connectivity in rural communities, increasing AI training opportunities, strengthening the enforcement of digital regulations, and integrating cyber security measures into national development strategies.
evidence_items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION: ASSESSING THE DRIVERS OF TECHNOLOGICAL PROGRESS ACROSS INDUSTRIES IN IRAQ

evidence_items.summary: This dataset supports the study entitled “From Selection Response to Genomic Prediction: A Bibliometric and Content Analysis of Four Decades of Tilapia Breeding Research.” The package contains the processed bibliographic records derived from 390 Scopus records, descriptive summary tables, keyword frequency counts, a structured content-analysis table covering 43 selected studies, and a data dictionary. evidence_items.summary: Preliminary, time-stamped deposit of the study design for a methodological study in health evidence informatics. The work proposes and will validate a machine-learning-assisted screening method with stratum-conditional certified recall: recall is certified within each stratum of a document pool (a per-stratum lower confidence bound, with a union bound across strata for simultaneous validity), rather than only in aggregate. This version contains the study protocol and the search strategy documentation (master concept set; six databases — PubMed, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, ACM Digital Library, DOAJ; verbatim native strings; field scopes; counts; deviation notes). The literature search was executed on 16–17 October 2026; screening, the certified-recall method, and the analyses are prospective and not yet run. Further versions will add the final corpus and the full analysis code. As this is a methodological study (not a clinical systematic review), prospective registration in a registry such as PROSPERO does not apply.
evidence_items.title: A stratum-conditional certified-recall machine-learning-assisted screening method — Study protocol and search strategy (preliminary deposit)

evidence_items.summary: Soil fertility decline is one of the major causes of low performance of farming systems in Burkina Faso. This investigation focused on valorisation of local substrates as fertilizer, by evaluating the effects of different formulation of dried faecal sludge and Burkina phosphate on maize and cotton grown in rotation. The study was conducted at Matourkou (11°4′ et 11°6′ N, 4°19′ et 4°21′ W). The experimental design was a fisher bloc with six (6) treatments and four (4) replicates. The treatments included T1 (400 kg/ha BP); T2 (2500 kg/ha BVS); T3 (160 kg/ha BP + 1500 kg/ha BVS); T4 (120 kg/ha BP + 1750 kg/ha BVS); T5 (80 kg/ha BP + 2000 kg/ha BVS); T6 (37,5 kg/ha BP + 1750 kg/ha BVS + 687,8 kg/ha Montmorillonite clay + 12,5 kg/ha Ca((OH) 2 ). Maize and cotton high, root collar diameter, and yields were used for the determination of the effects of these treatments. As for the results, it’s only in the second year of the experiment that treatments T4 significantly improved yields of maize (60.33%) and cotton (and 109.1%) compared to the control (T1); it also improved dry biomass yield for both crops. These results indicate that the combination of dry faecal sludge and Burkina phosphate (T4) improved soil fertility and yields in a cotton-maize crop rotation system. This fertilization option can be considered for the sustainability of agricultural production systems while offering robust option for dry faecal sludge recycling. published by the Journal of Biodiversity and Environmental Sciences | JBES
evidence_items.title: Effects of dried faecal sludge fortified with various rates of Burkina phosphate powder on the growth and yields of maize and cotton cropped in a rotation system in western Burkina Faso

The package contains the annual extent series (2021-2026) for two management zones, interrupted time series estimates with placebo and covariate-adjusted specifications, a spatially explicit five-class reinvasion-risk index with full weight-sensitivity analysis, classification accuracy assessments, and the scripts that reproduce every reported quantity. Inputs are openly licensed satellite and geospatial products; the code is self-contained and deterministic.

evidence_items.summary: Local protocol success is not sufficient to close an agent service. We study when locally conformant protocol states justify relationship-level service closure across agent stacks. A protocol-neutral Agent Service Episode (ASE) separates capability, authority, commitment, process, authoritative external effect, evidence/acceptance, responsibility, and relationship state. The protocol corpus uses a specification snapshot cutoff of 15 September 2026. Two authors independently coded nine semantic-ownership dimensions. On 32 held-out cells, exact agreement was 78.1%, Cohen's $\kappa=0.566$ (bootstrap 95% CI $[0.295,0.815]$), and nominal Krippendorff's $\alpha=0.564$; the held-out sample contained no Delegated labels, so D/U reproducibility is not estimated. All six families natively own action/process semantics, but none owns or names an external owner for authoritative external effect or service closure at ASE scope; all 12 corresponding raw judgments were independently U/U. An Alloy upper-bound model shows that the strongest observed local semantics do not entail ASE closure. An integrated binding model establishes bounded joint realizability and single-removal non-redundancy, with D0 used as an encoding-alignment regression. An executable Agent Service Binding Profile demonstrates the same bindings on invariant-targeted CAD/CAE/PLM traces in a coverage/feasibility study. Thus, within this protocol snapshot, $\mathsf{TaskCompleted}$ does not by itself license $\mathsf{Closed}$. For Agentic Services Computing, service closure is a first-class cross-layer governance decision whose owner and validation rule must be explicit.
evidence_items.title: Where Agent Protocols Stop: Cross-Layer Gaps in Authority, Commitment, Evidence, and Service Closure

evidence_items.summary: This descriptive-comparative study examined innovative human resource management (HRM) strategies among food service establishments in Cauayan City, Isabela, Philippines, as a basis for an enhanced HRM framework. Using purposive sampling, the investigation surveyed 40 owners, HR managers, and employees associated with qualifying food service small and medium-sized enterprises. A structured questionnaire measured seven dimensions: flexible work systems and employee lifecycle, digital infrastructure and resource support, training and skill development, communication and motivation, employee well-being, health and safety, and organizational effectiveness and leadership. Frequency, percentage, weighted mean, independent-samples t-tests, and analysis of variance were used. Health and safety obtained the highest composite rating (3.43, very high), whereas communication, engagement, and motivation received the lowest (2.18, low). Organizational effectiveness and leadership (3.22), digital resource support (3.00), training (2.97), employee welfare (2.87), and flexible work systems (2.74) were rated high. Most demographic comparisons did not indicate statistically significant differences, although selected item-level exceptions were reported in the original thesis. The findings support an adaptive and resilient HRM framework linking employee safety, digital and flexible operations, workforce development, internal communication, and continuing evaluation. The survey captures respondents' ratings of practices, rather than directly establishing effects on productivity or causal effectiveness. The proposed framework offers a structured basis for managerial planning in food service SMEs under economic uncertainty.
evidence_items.title: Innovative Human Resource Management Strategies in the Food Service Industry: Basis for an Enhanced HRM Framework

evidence_items.summary: Perceived employability has become increasingly relevant in higher education as students evaluate not only the quality of their academic experience but also the extent to which their studies prepare them for transition into the labour market. This study examines the relationship between perceived employability and student satisfaction among undergraduate students in Greek higher education. A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed, using a structured questionnaire administered to 210 students in their fourth year of study or beyond at public universities in Northern Greece. Perceived employability and student satisfaction were assessed using established self-report scales. The participants reported moderate levels of perceived employability (M = 3.20, SD = 0.73) and relatively high levels of student satisfaction (M = 4.79, SD = 1.73). Perceived employability was positively and significantly associated with student satisfaction (r = .541, p < .001) and significantly predicted satisfaction, explaining 29.3% of its variance. No statistically significant differences in perceived employability or student satisfaction were identified according to gender or previous work experience and/or internship participation. The findings suggest that students’ perceptions of their future employment prospects are closely associated with their overall evaluation of the university experience, highlighting the relevance of employability-related development within higher education.
evidence_items.title: Perceived Employability and Student Satisfaction in Greek Higher Education: Evidence from University Students in Northern Greece

evidence_items.summary: Decentralized multi-robot shape formation in GPS-denied environments is important for search-and-rescue and disaster response. Conventional consensus-based formation controllers can violate safe separation, oscillate, or stall when communication degrades, sensors are noisy, or an agent drops out. This paper proposes a resilient decentralized controller that combines Huber-weighted consensus and Exponential Moving Average (EMA) state estimation with a Dual-Layer Artificial Potential Field (APF) safety barrier. The first layer adds an anti-symmetric lateral deflection to resolve head-on encounters between peers; the second applies a normal-plus-tangential circulation field around static obstacles. The framework is evaluated on five simulated nonholonomic differential-drive robots in Gazebo Harmonic (ROS 2 Jazzy). Three runs are compared: a linear consensus baseline, the same baseline under faults (15% packet loss, 50-150 ms delay, σ = 0.18 m sensor noise, and a mid-run agent blackout), and the proposed controller under the same faults. The fault-free baseline reached the pentagon fastest (0.0156 m final RMS error) but its minimum separation fell to 0.3918 m, with 31 logged violations of the 0.50 m margin. Under faults the baseline reached 0.0546 m with 5 violations (minimum 0.4833 m). The proposed controller recorded no violations, kept a minimum separation of 0.6757 m, and reached 0.0368 m final error, at the cost of slower convergence (about 21 s versus about 12-15 s). Results are from single simulation runs, and the safety barrier is empirical rather than formally guaranteed.
evidence_items.title: Resilient Decentralized Shape Formation of Multi-Robot Swarms Under Adversarial Real-World Faults in High-Complexity Disaster Environments

evidence_items.summary: A harness wraps one or more generators (language models, other neural models, programs or people) with a symbolic layer: a rule set and, optionally, a knowledge store. A checker evaluates each candidate output against the rules and returns a verdict and the violated rules. A release gate lets the output, or part of it, leave only when it passes or under an exception policy, fixed in advance or chosen per request. That is the minimal core. Optional modules, used alone or in any combination, extend it. Rules may filter inputs, decoding, finished outputs, agent actions before execution, and outputs already delivered. A failing output may be repaired by a minimal symbolic change, or revised under a budget the generator cannot alter, with the passing part released under caveats. A passing output may carry a receipt tied to the state it was checked against, so that a later change re-checks affected outputs and supersedes a receipt only when its verdict changes (or, optionally, when the facts it records change). The rule set may improve from evidence, each change held inactive until it passes a gate that can refuse unapproved weakening and require independent approval. Further modules separate claims from outcomes, count correlated sources once, re-extract rendered prose, replay decisions, accept statements by cost, add human review, and turn the harness's verdicts, repairs and revisions into training signals. Outputs may also be read into typed records before checking, with size caps and a per-rule estimate of evaluation work, or a step counter, so that each check made by a rule whose work can be estimated or counted is bounded in advance, and a request may bring rules of its own, written by the generator or another source and admitted only when they cannot relax the rules in force. Knowledge and policy changes can then be made in rules instead of model weights, and any fine-tuning that remains needs less manual labelling.
evidence_items.title: Rule-Gated Generation: A Harness That Filters, Repairs, Certifies and Re-Checks Machine-Generated Output and Improves Its Own Rules Under a Gate

evidence_items.summary: This study aims to examine gifted education programs according to the Educational and Learning Capital Model from the perspectives of teachers working with gifted students. The research followed a descriptive survey design. The study sample consisted of 260 teachers of gifted students from King Abdullah II Schools for Excellence and the Jubilee School. Two scales were developed; the first was used to examine gifted education programs according to the Educational Capital Model, and the second was used to examine gifted education programs through the Learning Capital Model. Together, the two scales comprised a total of 70 indicators based on the Educational and Learning Capital Approach (ELCA). Descriptive analysis used means and standard deviations. Teachers reported high levels of availability and use of educational and learning capitals. The mean value obtained from the first scale was 1.67 (SD = 0.274), while the mean value obtained from the second scale was 1.78 (SD = 0.258). Among the educational capitals, didactic educational capital ranked first, while infrastructural educational capital ranked last. Among the learning capitals, telic learning capital ranked first, while organismic learning capital ranked last. The assignment of a dedicated teacher to the innovation laboratory is recommended.
evidence_items.title: Evaluation of Gifted Programs According to the Educational and Learning Capital Model

evidence_items.summary: Data and analytical software for thermally activated Fe-SMA fibre-reinforced concrete This repository accompanies the article “Analytical modelling of thermally activated iron-based shape memory alloy fibre concrete: Finite transfer and capacity compatibility”. It provides the numerical source data, analytical implementation, calibration inputs, and results used to prepare the final article. The work examines finite fibre–matrix transfer, thermally activated composite response, cohesive-law identification, and the compatibility of reported strengths with uncertain fibre orientation and tensile capacity. The deposit contains one final analysis snapshot. It includes the reference formulation and the baselines, thermal alternatives, and cohesive-law candidates examined in the article. These are parts of the reported scientific assessment, rather than separate manuscript versions. Superseded model results, development archives, manuscript drafts, and unrelated source files are excluded. Contents • data/ contains numerical representations of published response curves, reported group statistics, study metadata, fixed constituent and pullout calibrations, optimizer initialization values, and published experimental/finite-element comparison curves. Curve identifiers preserve the link to the source study and figure. These are processed publication-based data, rather than original instrument records. • model/ contains the executable analysis scripts. They fit the concrete and composite controls, evaluate reference responses and competing baselines, compare response curves on matched displacement grids, assess orientation and conditional envelopes, test capacity compatibility, verify the independent finite-transfer solver, and fit/test the nested cohesive laws. model/screen capacity.py provides a command-line conditional strength screen.
evidence_items.title: Data and analytical models for thermally activated Fe-SMA fibre-reinforced concrete: Finite transfer, cohesive response and capacity compatibility
